doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Jingle work and the Sing Sing Sing edit
summary: Clarinet jingles and one absurd Sing Sing Sing recreation session.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Do you ever get calls for classical dates in New York?
Once in a while, not so much now, because that’s a whole closed — I do get calls to do a lot of jingles, ads, I’m on a lot of those, things like that. They use a lot of clarinets on those things.
What was the most silliest sounding jingle you’ve done? Is that possible to remember?

Well they did, there was a guy — a few years ago they used a Benny Goodman record on a Chase Manhattan bank commercial. And these ad agencies always like to imitate each other. If something is popular they all do it. So then all the clarinet players were getting calls. And they always wanted to do a recreation of “Sing Sing Sing” or something like that. But one guy had me and a drummer come in, and he had taken the old Carnegie Hall record of “Sing Sing Sing” and edited it the way he wanted it. And he wanted us to recreate this edit. But he had no sense of time. So the edit was chopped up so the drums would play like a bar and a half and then the clarinet would come in. It didn’t make any sense at all. And this is what he wanted us to play. There was no music written, and this guy was probably getting thousands and thousands of dollars for being the composer of this jingle. And it sounded about as goofy as it sounds from me telling it.
You were able to do what he wanted?
We were able to do it, we took hours in the studio trying to do this. It could have been done so easily.
Right. If he had gotten someone in to just advise him.

Yes. If he actually did his work and wrote something. Instead he plays us a cassette tape of — it was a real backwards way. Because when you do jingles you’re supposed to match, they always want to match phrases with if there’s an edit or a cut, they want to match it so it fits that. So instead of writing it, he chopped up a tape and that’s what he wanted us to do. But we got paid for all those hours we were there. So that’s okay.
